items.item_text: BS degree in Plant Genetics, Plant Breeding, Biotechnology, or related field of study.
MS degree in Plant Genetics, Plant Breeding, Biotechnology, or related field of study, or equivalent experience.

Minimum of 5 years of experience in a molecular biology or genetics laboratory with demonstrated basic genetics or molecular biology laboratory skills [e.g., micropipetting, nucleic acid isolation, polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and nucleic acid quantification] and operation of specialized laboratory equipment (e.g., a capillary electrophoresis sequencer/genetic analyzer).

Preferred 2 years of experience in a molecular biology or genetics laboratory with demonstrated specialized skills of genotyping clonal crops using microsatellite markers and capillary electrophoresis for plant variety identification.

Under general supervision, provide technical support in the Foundation Plant Services (FPS) Plant Identification Laboratory by conducting variety identification testing of FPS Foundation Greenhouse grapevines and evaluating new marker systems for use in variety identification. Work closely with colleagues to coordinate and lead FPS identification testing efforts utilizing microsatellite markers and capillary electrophoresis (CE). Independently analyze and review raw CE data using custom fragment analysis genotyping software and report results. Evaluate non-microsatellite markers and data to improve variety identification. Support routine sampling and testing throughout the year of vineyards, orchards, greenhouse plants and newly introduced plant materials. Multiple and diverse projects will be coordinated concurrently.
75% - DNA-Based Variety ID Of Dept Collections
15% - Design And Conduct Research On DNA ID FPS Crops
5% - DNA-Based Variety ID Of External ID Client Samples
5% - Maintain An Efficient And Effective Lab
Specialized knowledge of genetics and molecular biology of clonal specialty crops with an emphasis on genotyping and variety identification of grapevines and temperate fruit and nut trees.

Demonstrated ability to work in a flexible manner under the pressure created in an active service/academic environment while keeping detailed, accurate, neat and legible experimental records, including effective and efficient use of cloud-based file sharing, such as Box or OneDrive.

Ability to analyze plant variety identification results from molecular marker data for validity, including researching variety information from available variety databases, pedigrees, plant patents, and other records.
Ability to write competitive grants applications to fund research, annual reports for the funded grants, and scientific papers for publication in peer reviewed journals.

Demonstrated ability to process and interpret capillary electrophoresis fragment analysis data to recognize irregular or invalid results, assess and troubleshoot results to correct or modify techniques using independent judgement and originality.

Demonstrated ability to integrate assigned priorities with time, equipment, and material requirements necessary to execute diverse protocols and maintain documentation while adhering to established laboratory safety requirements.
Ability to critically evaluate scientific literature to understand and adopt or adapt new methodologies to improve both research and service programs.
